messages:
Tara: heads up — APAC client latencies spiking, lots of 502s for streaming endpoints. started ~07:15 UTC. looks like GeoDNS fallback sent more traffic to us-west and our egress SNAT pool is getting hammered.
Sam: copy, can you paste the dashboard link?
Tara: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/egress/apac-to-usw - 95th jumped from 120ms to 700ms, error rate ~3.4% :confused:
Raj: got the alert too. quick check on nat metrics shows ephemeral ports near saturation on the us-west nat-gw nodes. conntrack entries spiking.
Marta: do we have recent changes to region pinning or geo weights? I didn't deploy anything but Platform did tweak a TTL for geoDNS yesterday.
Tara: yeah TTL moved from 30s -> 10s yesterday (to speed failovers). might be causing faster churn and more cross-region flows.
Raj: repro of conntrack dump (abridged):
```
# kubectl -n infra exec -it nat-gw-02 -- conntrack -S | head -n 6
entries: 64312
expect-nf_conntrack_bucket_ratio: 0.50
hashsize: 32768
hashmask: 32767
```
and active ports per instance: ~62k / 64k
Marta: 64k ephemeral ports is the limit, we hit it. two choices: increase sources (NAT nodes) or reduce cross-region flows.
Sam: short-term: can we increase nat-gw count and bump conntrack? medium-term: revert TTL change and add hysteresis to geo-DNS so we don't oscillate.
Tara: ops-oncall-bot shows a few lb nodes with high TIME_WAIT. also see haproxy keepalive low. maybe our LB settings accelerate port churn.
Marta: config snippets to change:
```
haproxy:
  tcp-keepalive: 300
  maxconns: 20000
kernel:
  net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max: 262144
```
Raj: I'm spinning a couple extra nat-gw instances (us-west) now and raising conntrack to 262k on them. will monitor.
ops-oncall-bot: alert: NAT_PORT_EXHAUSTION (us-west) - 12:18 UTC - current_ports=62114 - threshold=62000 - triggered_by=conntrack
Sam: can we also tweak GeoDNS weights to favor us-east for APAC until capacity stabilizes? that lowers cross-region RTT but costs more egress. tradeoff ok short-term?
Marta: prefer partial pins per route: pin streaming endpoints to nearest region, and allow batch/rerank jobs to fallback. easier to scale for the streaming surface.
Tara: agree. for immediate mitigation: 1) add 2 nat-gw nodes in us-west (Raj) 2) bump conntrack & haproxy keepalive (Raj/Marta) 3) revert geoTTL to 30s + add 60s hysteresis (Marta) 4) temporary geo weight adjustment favoring us-east for APAC (Sam)
Raj: started nodes, conntrack updated, haproxy keepalive change queued — rolling patch with zero-downtime.
Marta: I'll open infra PR for geoDNS hysteresis logic and pin policy per-route. rough patch: add "grace_window": 60s in geo policy.
Sam: also add monitoring alert for TIME_WAIT surge and a runbook link: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/nat-port-exhaustion
Tara: thanks. keeping this thread for post-mortem notes. if spikes persist we'll consider reserving dedicated egress pool for high-throughput APAC traffic. :eyes:
ops-oncall-bot: incident updated: mitigations applied, monitoring at 12:28 UTC.
Tara: will check dashboards in 10m and report back.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Marta: adding follow-up: cost impact estimate for extra egress + cross-region traffic, will share by EOD.
Tara: noted, closing for now unless errors recur.
